records.title: This Slinky Can Walk Forever!
records.source: public caption text via youtubetotranscript.com (rendered from YouTube captions)
records.script: This is a slinky and this is the world's first infinite slinky staircase. And I made it because as a kid, I would always try and see how many stairs I could get my slinky to climb down. With my record sadly always maxing out at seven or eight, I decided now that I'm an engineer, it was time to avenge this childhood frustration to set an unbeatable world record. The first thought I had was using a treadmill tilted at just the right angle. The problem with that is there was very little repeatability. because the landing surfaces were inclined unlike actual stairs. To solve that issue, I tried an actual escalator. And although that worked a little better, the distance between the steps wasn't ideal and the speed was a little too slow. That's why we just decided to make our own prototype of an escalator I could turn with a hand crank. And that prototype worked well because we got the stairs spacing dialed in. But we were having issues keeping the slinky aligned, which is where these 3D printed self centering cones came in handy. Because if we put one on each stair step, the slinky would self align and then be in the perfect position to fall to the next step. And after a few last minute adjustments and replacing the hand crank with an actual motor, we made the final version to test if we could beat my childhood record of eight steps. Alright, It's been 48 hours and I'm happy to report this slinky has climbed 208,000 stairs, which is 29,000 times more than I ever got as a kid.

records.title: I accidentally killed this magnet
records.source: public caption text via youtubetotranscript.com (rendered from YouTube captions)
records.script: What I have here is just a really strong neodymium magnet, and a while ago I decided to see what would happen, if I blasted it with a blowtorch. It honestly didn't look like it did very much, but what was interesting was that once it had cooled down, it was no longer a magnet, and it was just a heavy piece of junk. This was all just an excuse though, to test out this really expensive and kind of scary machine, that I ordered from China. In theory it was supposed to be able to revive the magnet, and I just had to wait for it to charge up to 2000V. Then after that I just put this cloth thing over this other thing, shoved my little cube into the hole, and when I was ready I clicked the button. After that I pulled it out and inside it still looked exactly the same, but this time when I tested it, there was definitely a big difference. Oh my God... In fact it was somehow even stronger than when I started, and I'd apparently accidentally upgraded it.

records.title: Why do Rivers Curve?
records.source: public caption text via youtubetotranscript.com (rendered from YouTube captions)
records.script: As long as nothing gets in the way of a river's meandering, its curves will continue to grow curvier and curvier. Until they loop around and bumble into themselves. When that happens, the rivers channel follow the straighter path downhill, leaving behind a crescent-shaped remnant called an 'Oxbow Lake'.

records.title: Newton's Cradle Explained
records.source: public caption text via youtubetotranscript.com (rendered from YouTube captions)
records.script: If I take three balls out of this Newton's cradle and let it go, will we have three balls come out the other side? There's only two left. In a closed system without any external forces acting, momentum always stays exactly the same. And a great example of this is this system of bowling balls we have suspended from the ceiling, sometimes called a Newton's cradle. If I take one ball out of this Newton's cradle and let it go, when it collides exactly one ball will come out the other side with exactly the same speed. What happens if we take more? Say we take the mass of three balls? Momentum needs to stay the same, but only two balls are left. So if we have three balls going in, three come up. The momentum of the middle one keeps the same. The only way to change the momentum in a closed system is to add an external force.
